data.title: French economy contracts more than expected in third quarter
data.description:
France's economy contracted by 0.2% in the third quarter, final data from statistics office INSEE showed on Friday, more than the preliminary estimate for a 0.1% decline.

The contraction in the euro zone's second-largest economy was also below the average forecast of -0.1% in a Reuters poll of 22 economists.

  • Exports fell 1.6%, after rising 2.9% in the previous quarter

  • Household consumption rose 0.3%, compared with a 0.2% increase in the second quarter

  • A decline in investment sped up to 0.9% after falling 0.5% in the previous three months

  • INSEE said annual carry-over growth stood at 0.1% at the end of the third quarter

  • The Bank of France said earlier in November that the economy should avoid a recession and return to "moderate" growth in the fourth quarter

data.title: AI Equity Selloff Likely Had Limited Impact on Asian Economies — Market Talk
data.description: The recent artificial intelligence-related equity selloff has yet to make a dent in Asia's exports, ANZ Research analysts say in a report. South Korea's first 20-day export data for November shows demand continues to be strong, driven by semiconductors. Vietnam's export data for the first half of November also depict robust demand. "Hence, this suggests that the AI selloff is currently a financial-market shock and not a real-economy shock," ANZ says. The region is supported by existing orders and production schedules in the near-term, they add. However, ANZ notes that scheduled orders for 2027 or 2028, depend on whether companies remain willing and able to finance enormous investment needed to build the AI infrastructure.(amanda.lee@wsj.com)

data.title: Indian firms utilising only 20%-30% of free trade agreement benefits, RBI governor says
data.description:
Indian businesses are using only about 20%-30% of the benefits available under free-trade agreements (FTAs) compared with their foreign counterparts, Reserve Bank of India Governor Sanjay Malhotra said at an event in Mumbai on Friday.

The comments come days after Prime Minister Narendra Modi said ⁠Indian industry should take advantage of opportunities from the free-trade agreements India has signed, including those with the EU and the UK

"The government of India has now opened up a number of avenues. A number of FTAs have been signed. At the same time, however, it has been found that only about 20% to 30% of the utilization has been done by Indians vis-à-vis 60% to 70% by our partners in the trade agreements," Malhotra said at an event for small and medium businesses

There is a long way to go for Indian businesses to take advantage of the lower tariffs negotiated under the agreements, he said

Small and medium businesses should learn more about the FTAs to improve quality, delivery timelines, standards and certifications, Malhotra added

The micro, small and medium enterprises sector has an AI adoption rate of about 14%, behind peers such as China, Malhotra said

India has free-trade agreements with the UK, Oman and New Zealand. Its proposed free-trade agreement with the European Union is expected to accelerate market-access opportunities and investment ⁠flows between India and the ⁠27-member EU bloc

Separately, India's Trade Minister Piyush Goyal said on Friday that India and the US were close to wrapping up a long-anticipated trade deal

PM Modi told industry leaders last week that Indian businesses could not take their huge domestic market for granted and urged them to compete globally in an era when resources were being weaponised.

data.title: Eurozone Bond Yields Track Treasury Yields, Oil Prices Higher — Market Talk
data.description: Eurozone government bond yields rise on what is shaping up to be a busy day for issuance and data. Upward pressure on yields comes from rising U.S. Treasury yields and higher oil prices. Italy will hold an up to 8 billion euro auction of 2032- and 2036-dated nominal bonds, or BTPs, and 2034- and 2035-dated floating-rate notes, or CCTeu. The day has already delivered flash estimate French and Spanish inflation data for November, among other data. The 10-year German Bund yield rises 2.4 basis points to 3.281%, while yields on peer eurozone 10-year bonds rise less than that, according to Tradeweb. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)

data.title: Taiwan raises 2026 GDP growth projection to 13.28% on strong AI demand
data.description:
Key points:
  • 2026 GDP estimate +13.28 vs previous +11.05%
  • 2026 CPI estimate +2.07% vs previous +2.07%
  • 2027 GDP forecast +6.51% vs previous +6.04%

Taiwan's economy is expected to expand by 13.28% in 2026, the Directorate General of Budget, Accounting and Statistics said on Friday, raising its outlook from a previous estimate of 11.05%, boosted by strong AI demand.

Taiwan plays a leading role in fulfilling the demand for AI chips and technology from firms like Nvidia and Apple , with the island being home to the world's largest contract chip manufacturer, Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co .

Demand for AI already drove Taiwan's economy in 2025 to expand 8.76%.

The agency also revised up its third-quarter 2026 economic growth view to 14.39% from a preliminary reading of 14.36%.

For next year, it said it expected Taiwan's economy to grow 6.51%, upgrading its August prediction of 6.04%.

data.title: Carl Icahn's wealth takes a hit as debt pressures mount, CVR Energy slumps
data.description:
Carl Icahn, the billionaire hedge fund manager and activist investor, has seen his fortune shrink in recent years amid mounting debt pressures.

Earlier this month, Icahn Enterprises said there can be no assurance it will be able to refinance $1.4B of bonds due in May "on acceptable terms or at all." Yields on these bonds have climbed to over 14% from ~6% three months ago.

Shares of CVR Energy , a key IEP holding, dropped around 46% since the company agreed to buy two oil refineries in the U.S. CVR accounted for about half of IEP's publicly traded investment portfolio as of the end of Sept.

Yields on some of IEP's 2029 bonds now exceed 30%, Bloomberg News reported this week. IEP has ~$4.4B of bonds outstanding.

All of these factors have strained Icahn's fortune, which fell to $1.2B last week, the lowest since Bloomberg began tracking his wealth in 2012. His net worth, which peaked at $26.1B in Dec. 2013, is down ~$20B over the past five years.

Icahn has ~$1.3B of personal loans, largely secured by IEP units that lost ~66% of their value in the past six months.

IEP's private investment vehicles — which deploy capital belonging to IEP, Icahn and his family — lost 31% in Q3. The funds' long positions were down $170M and short positions fell $610M.

S&P Global in Aug. downgraded IEP's credit rating, saying persistent losses in investment funds continued to weaken its business position.

"Since 2019, the funds have had annual losses, except for 2025, which saw a modest positive return," S&P said. "We anticipate that IEP's cash flow adequacy will remain under pressure over the next 12-18 months."

S&P said it expects IEP  to successfully refinance as needed, but its weak financial performance hurt its general standing in the capital markets over the last few years.
